A long time ago I used to be fat, with a BMI of 28. One day, I decided to become a normal human and stop eating like a pig. Healthy foods from then on.

I wasn't one of those "hey everyone look at me I'm consuming the right food that any regular guy would" people. I was quiet about it. But people noticed, I'd order salads without dressing, I'd eat much less at gatherings, etc. Naturally, my overweight friends noticed.

I was good friends with my landlords two sons. One was a little pushy, telling me I was starving myself in a sarcastic tone, etc. the other actually made fun of me. This guy was BIG, like 6'3", 2xx pounds. Active as hell, but then he'd eat an entire medium pizza to himself when he got home. I'd make myself lunch, and take it to my room, on the way he would always ask "what are you eating?" in a mocking voice. "Food." I always responded. He'd then get annoyed and stand up, walk over to me, and look at what I'm eating with a smirk on his face then go sit back down.

One day, I managed to close my door after my usual response of "Food." I hear heavy footsteps getting louder. My door crashes open. "Ew. An avocado. Really??" More smirking. He slams the door and returns to the company he was entertaining at the time.

TL;DR: Started to eat way healthier. Fat friend would run up to me to smirk at the food I was eating. He even busted into my room once to tell me avocados were gross.

I have been thinking about it since they've introduced the YouTube License.

As far as I remember it, before this license you just had to give proper credits and you could do pretty much whatever you want.

I believe the Monstercat License was introduced to make the process uniform. It was messy before, and you often did not get a response. Now, you are guaranteed to get it as long as you pay up.

Interesting way to look at it, I still believe that it would be better off if they would allow everyone to freely make videos and stream using their material.

I mean, all those million+ subs YouTubers and eSports streamers with 300k+ viewers is free advertisement, you don't want to push them to your competitor.
I guess if you view it that way, it could be viewed as a money grubbing move. With no true competitors (what similar service can you think of?), they raised the price.
In addition, there are also small time YouTubers making videos using Monstercat, I don't think that they want to spend 15$ per month to prevent getting striked.
They won't get struck, only claimed. Small Youtubers can still use the music, they just won't be able to monetize it.
Lets hope that they won't push more extreme methods, I have seen plenty companies do everything to squeeze out an extra buck.
Remember that Monstercat does not prevent creators from using its music. The license only allows a ytber or a streamer to make money from the content using the music (like a video).

Disclosure, I mod /v/nostupidquestions (NSQ) and this proposal would benefit the sub. Though I honestly think it would benefit both subs.

To improve the quality of AskVoat, I suggest you bring the rules and enforcement more in line with a similar sub on another site. There, you can't ask closed ended questions or questions with definitive answers. All questions must prompt discussion and a variety of answers. A lot of AskVoat questions are effectively tech support for how to use Voat. Examples:

  • Is there a way to group my subscriptions?
  • What is the name of our mascot?
  • Is there a subverse to asvertise subverses
  • What's the difference between "my sets" and "front"?

Others have simple answers that would not invite lots of answers from various people. Examples:

  • Why does my bellybutton stink and of I poke it to hard will my intestines fall out?
  • As an American, how would I move to Canada?
  • Why are BuzzFeed "correspondents" showing up on NPR?

NSQ would be a fine place for people to ask these sorts of questions. They'll get a simple answer from subscribers specifically looking to answer these types of questions. While AskVoat subscribers can have the thought provoking questions and answers they presumably expect and want.

If any of your mods would like to join the mod team of NSQ that would be great, it's not a power grab. I think this would really help out both subs. In addition, if you wanted assistance enforcing this and directing people to NSQ, I'd be willing to help mod AskVoat, patrolling the new queue.

Thanks!
Idea: start removing closed ended questions as well as questions with a definitive answer and directing those people to /v/nostupidquestions

While the second type of question is something I want to keep on AskVoat as there could still be discussion about the best way to go to Canada, where to go and why etc. and there could be a critical analysis provoking discussion on NPR because of the third question. Also, it will be hard to draw a clear line and users won't like it if their post is deemed too simple.

On the first type of questions it seems that they never get a lot of points or complaints, but I don't like seeing them on /v/askvoat and the community wouldn't mind those questions being sent to /v/nostupidquestions. For now I will just put it in the sidebar, unless the other mods want to make a rule out of it. Thanks for the suggestion.

Dang, we are getting hammered with these questions. And they are all getting fast answers. Thanks a lot -- hopefully it's good for you guys, too.

If you have other undesirable questions in the future, feel free to direct people to us!
Didn't expect it would be so effective, thanks for suggesting it.
